The concept is called Judicial Notice. It is not really meant to be applied to something like the Holocaust. It's more about the Court accepting as true things like recorded deeds and court orders and judgments without someone having to testify as to the truth and accuracy of the documents. I suppose the Court could take judicial notice of the holocaust if the truth or falsity of the holocaust wasn't the sole factual issue in the case that needed to be resolved, but in this case, it's literally the only issue in the case. The thing is, even if the Court were to take judicial notice of a document, you could always object to the Court doing so if you think the document is a forgery or fraud. So for instance, if the Court takes judicial notice of a deed that has been recorded, all thats really being admitted into evidence is the fact that the county recorders office has a deed recorded on file. Whether or not that deed is valid, enforceable, etc., is a different question and the Court would not take judicial notice of such a fact. So if the Court attempts to take judicial notice of "the holocaust" there's nothing to stop you from presenting evidence to contradict the mainstream narrative and if you can show there is a possibility of a legitimate factual dispute. I suppose a Court could readily take judicial notice of historical accounts of the holocaust, but in the same way that you could still challenge the veracity of a deed, you can dispute that those accounts are accurate.
